summary: Request exemption: higher burst limit for enterprise chat route (/v1/chat/completions) during market-open traffic spikes
description:
Issue summary
Proxima Bank is requesting a temporary increase to their burst allowance on the enterprise-protected chat route (/v1/chat/completions) in eu-west. They report predictable short spikes at market open (08:55–09:10 local) where they see elevated 429s despite overall sustained RPS being within their contracted baseline.

Customer request
- Increase burst capacity (token bucket burst) for /v1/chat/completions in eu-west.
- Keep sustained rate unchanged (they are not asking for a permanent throughput increase).
- They want the change to apply only to their tenant + route group (no broader tier default changes).

Impact observed (customer)
- During spikes, client sees 429 responses with reason=quota_exceeded and occasionally reason=overload_admission when the region is under pressure.
- Primary business impact is delayed responses for end-user chat assistant at market open; they can tolerate some throttling but want fewer hard 429s during the first 10–15 minutes.

Environment
- Hosted API (enterprise tier)
- Region: eu-west
- Route: /v1/chat/completions
- Model: rw-chat-large (pinned)
- Client uses streaming; retries are currently immediate (no jitter) per their current implementation.

Qualification notes (Support/CS)
- Customer is enterprise with explicit latency/availability SLO expectations.
- Pattern appears bursty and time-bounded; sustained usage is stable.
- Customer can implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter, but wants Redwood-side burst adjustment as primary mitigation.

Risk assessment (internal)
- Increasing burst allowance can shift pressure onto shared enterprise GPU pools during localized demand spikes.
- Must avoid degrading other protected enterprise tenants on the same route group.
- Exception must be scoped (tenant + route + region), time-boxed, and monitored.
- Must keep decision auditable and reversible (feature-flag/config driven; clear rollback criteria).

Requested outcome
- Approve a time-limited burst exemption with guardrails and monitoring, plus customer guidance to add retry backoff/jitter and concurrency caps.

Attachments/References
- Customer provided sample timestamps and request IDs in email to TAM; copied into internal comment thread below.
- Related to earlier burst event tracking in SUP-18433 (latency + shedding correlation).

Customer (Proxima Bank) asking for higher burst on /v1/chat/completions (eu-west). They can live with same sustained but want fewer 429s in first ~15 min of trading day. They shared a sample from today: 08:57–09:04 saw ~6–9% 429s. Request IDs: rwreq_9f2c… rwreq_aa31… (sent via email). Please advise if we can grant a scoped exception and how to message this alongside client-side backoff.

2026-01-18 10:05 (Aisha Bello)
From SRE perspective: OK to consider a time-boxed burst exemption if we keep it tenant-scoped and monitor shed/admission. Please ensure we don’t raise tier defaults. Provide rollback trigger: if enterprise p95 latency burn > 1.5x baseline for 10 min or overload_admission for other tenants increases.

2026-01-18 10:47 (Amara Diallo)

Also: please ensure customer parses Retry-After and uses jitter; immediate retries amplify the burst bucket depletion.

2026-01-18 11:10 (Owen Phillips)

- Sustained RPS outside the window is within baseline; peak is ~2.6–2.9x baseline for 2–6 minutes.

Conclusion: a burst exception is likely to reduce the majority of their 429s during market open. It will not eliminate overload_admission when the region is under protection, but those events are rare in their traces.

Product approval: OK with a temporary burst exemption for Proxima provided it is:
1) tenant + route + region scoped,
2) time-boxed (2 weeks) with renewal requiring review,
3) accompanied by customer action items (backoff/jitter, concurrency limits),
4) documented in ticket with explicit rollback criteria.

Please tag SRE lead for final go/no-go.

SRE approval with guardrails.

Please coordinate change window outside market open if possible and annotate dashboards.

Resolution: Approved and applied a tenant/route/region-scoped burst multiplier increase (2.0x -> 3.0x) for Proxima Bank on /v1/chat/completions in eu-west for 14 days (auto-expiring 2026-02-02). Customer advised on proper retry/backoff and concurrency limits. Monitoring shows reduced quota-based 429s with no adverse impact to other enterprise traffic.
resolution: Temporary burst exemption approved and implemented. Burst allowance for Proxima Bank (enterprise) on /v1/chat/completions in eu-west increased from 2.0x to 3.0x sustained rate, with no sustained quota change. Scope is tenant + route group + region; TTL auto-expires 2026-02-02 07:00 UTC. Customer instructed to honor Retry-After and implement exponential backoff with jitter + concurrency caps. No billing changes. Monitoring after rollout shows significant reduction in quota_exceeded 429s and no measurable degradation for other protected enterprise traffic.
